name: Transformer vs Circuit Breaker
instruction: Create a 3D model comparing a transformer and a circuit breaker. The transformer should have a rectangular body with cylindrical coils on top. The circuit breaker should be a small rectangular box with a switch on the front. Place them side by side for comparison.

Shape accuracy: The transformer has a rectangular body.
The transformer features cylindrical coils on top.
The circuit breaker is a small rectangular box.
The switch on the circuit breaker is clearly defined.
Color representation: The color set in the script is reasonable for the object.
Size: The size set in the script is reasonable for the object.
Proportion: The coils are proportionate to the body of the transformer.
The box is at a reasonable height relative to the circuit breaker.
Texture and surface detail: The texture and surface detail set in the script is reasonable for the object.

Three-dimensional spatial awareness: The transformer is positioned with its coils clearly visible.
The circuit breaker is placed at an appropriate height for comparison.
Both objects are aligned side by side for clear visibility.
Object distance and contact: There is adequate space between the transformer and the circuit breaker.
The positioning allows for easy visual comparison without overlap.

Instruction execution accuracy: Both the transformer and circuit breaker are accurately represented.
The placement side by side is correctly executed.
